speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help you, I will need to ask some questions and may order tests. First, is your baby currently having trouble breathing right now, and do they have a history of choking or a foreign object being placed in their mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with secondary Gastroesophageal Reflux (GERD).

The combination of inspiratory stridor that worsens with neck flexion and feeding, along with post-prandial vomiting, is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the recurrent nature and associated vomiting, I will now order a pH-impedance study to evaluate for reflux severity and rule out aspiration pneumonia.
